analysis.title: Global Rates Weekly: Start of rates bite
key_insights: BofA says rising rates are starting to tighten broader financial conditions, with spread widening in French OATs, EU periphery and US high yield. Central banks are pushing back, but data (NFP, EU and AU CPI) will likely drive near-term moves.
September saw large global rate moves. US 2s10s moved +50bp, a 2x 10Y standard-deviation move, and other regions moved 1-1.5x. Cuts priced for Q1 have become 100bp+ of hikes in most regions.

BofA stays paid 2Y UST and in curve flatteners. It reset the stop on its 2s30s flattener to 100bp after being stopped out of the nominal flattener. Its view is that the Fed faces a choice between hiking and a bond spike unless financial conditions tighten.

BofA economists expect Sept NFP of 60k (private 50k) vs Bloomberg consensus of 85k, with unemployment steady at 4.1%. A print at or below 60k would likely bull steepen the curve and cut terminal Fed pricing from 4.7% to 4.55-4.6%. A print above consensus would bear flatten and could push terminal pricing to 4.8%+.

A 3.0% core PCE print, mostly due to a method change, gives the Fed room to move slower. The standard Taylor rule now implies a peak fed funds rate of 4.8%, close to market pricing. The real fed funds history approach implies a 5.5% terminal rate.

BofA sees the market reaction to dovish comments from NY Fed's Williams and Fed Governor Jefferson as overdone. It argues rates are not yet sufficiently restrictive, and that Williams' 'no need for urgency' and Jefferson's 'more time' comment are premature ahead of Sept NFP and CPI.

The 2s30s steepening is almost entirely real-rate driven. BofA attributes it to elevated uncertainty, limited client interest in fading the move, hedging flows, soft auctions and the MOVE index spike.

Rates vol and the RV de-risking led UST to take the full $6b in the 10-20y buyback. Offers were $46b vs a $19b historical average, the largest long-end buyback offering. BofA says this reflects liquidity support, not an aggressively bid UST.

BofA expects the midterms to be a muted event for rates. Split Congress is the base case. A Democratic sweep would give a 2Y move of -5 to -7bp and 10Y of -3 to -5bp. A Republican sweep would give 2Y of +7 to +10bp and 10Y of +3 to +5bp, with bear flattening on fiscal easing risk.

The 10y OAT-Bund spread widened 30bp+ in four days to 140bp, about 10bp off sovereign crisis levels. BofA names six drivers: stops on longs, negative convexity flows, month-end portfolio shifts, 2027 supply concerns, political noise and bearish technicals. It estimates fair value at 100-110bp and the spread looks about 33-42bp too wide on its models.

BofA technicals show OAT 10Y yield could reach about 5.54% on Fibonacci extension, and BTP-Bund and SPGB-Bund could catch up toward about 185bp and 100bp. It lists five backstops that would prevent OAT-Bunds above 150bp: lower WAM of supply, more cautious parties, domestic buying, periphery-to-OAT flows and ECB action.
BofA cut its French growth forecasts to 0.3% this year and 0.6% next year (-10bp and -20bp), and warns of a feedback loop between financing costs, growth and deficits.

RBA hiked 25bp to 4.60%, a 15-year high, but the press conference was viewed as dovish and trimmed mean CPI came in at 0.24% m/m vs BofA's 0.38% forecast. Market pricing fell to 7bp for November and about 36bp by mid-2027. BofA stays paid Nov RBA OIS (current 7bp, risk lower oil) and closed the 1y2y AU vs ESTR trade at its stop.

10y ACGB yields are around 5.4%, the highest since 2011. BofA sees no meaningful rally until domestic data slow, which it does not expect before 1Q27, but expects AU rates to keep outperforming the US.

BofA argues the rise in long-end JGB yields is a global spillover (10Y UST at 5.25%, a 19-year high) rather than Japan-specific. Net JGB supply falls from ¥6.5tn in Q3 to ¥5.6tn in Q4 2026. The 40Y auction bid-to-cover of 3.10x was the highest since July 2020. BofA prefers long 30y JGB ASW (entry 45bp, target 35bp, stop 52bp, current 49bp) over outright longs.

US 3-6m T-bills have cheapened as money market funds shun intermediate bills amid Fed path and bill supply uncertainty. BofA expects them to stay cheap, sees upside risk to bill supply, and sees strong FRN demand that supports a 1Y FRN issuance.
BofA expects BoE reserves to stay near £640bn through YE26 and decline to £615bn by YE27, with £20bn a year of Gilt sales starting April 2027. It stays long UKT 0.875% 2033 on asset swap.

Rates vol has repriced higher in a roughly even split between higher forwards and a logVol normalization (c.18.1% to c.20.7%). On 1y10y normal vol, 11bp of the 21bp rise came from the logVol reset. BofA sees limited room for vol to normalize without a duration rally and sees the best opportunity to fade the sell-off and vol as backloaded into November (US midterms, UST refunding).

BofA's technicals team says the 2026 US real-yield breakout resembles Jan-2022, when SPX, EURUSD and Bitcoin peaked and equity, rates and FX vol rose. It suggests considering 1-3m SPY puts or a put spread for protection.

BofA forecasts: Fed funds 4.375% at YE26 and YE27, 10Y UST 5.00% at YE26 and 4.75% at YE27, ECB refi 2.90% at YE26 and 2.40% at YE27, BoJ 1.50% at YE26 and 2.00% at YE27, BoE 4.00% at YE26 and 4.25% at YE27, RBA 4.60% at YE26 and 4.10% at YE27.

trade_ideas.rationale: Fed seeking a restrictive stance, with rates not yet sufficiently restrictive.
trade_ideas.risk: Economic slowdown or slowing jobs while inflation stabilizes.

trade_ideas.rationale: Long-end USTs supported by Fed inflation credibility, and a Fed that hikes to contain the bond sustains a flattening bias.
trade_ideas.risk: Dovish Fed pivot and UST stops on long-end support.

trade_ideas.description: Long 2y and 30y UST asset swap spreads (ASW). 30y entered 19-Aug-26 at -71bp, target -55bp, stop -80bp, latest -67bp
trade_ideas.rationale: Favorable carry on the 2y and buybacks richening long-end USTs vs swaps.
trade_ideas.risk: Higher rates vol pressuring spread widening, higher future bill issuance, major risk-off liquidity crunch.

trade_ideas.description: Long 10y20y inflation swap, entered 8-Sep-26 at 2.35%, target 2.55%, stop 2.20%
trade_ideas.rationale: Fed waits for inflation deterioration before tightening, so Fed credibility is at risk.
trade_ideas.risk: Equity selloff and poor long-end liquidity.

trade_ideas.description: Pay Nov RBA OIS, entered 23-Sep-26 at 9bp, target 25bp, stop 3bp, latest 7.6bp
trade_ideas.rationale: November remains a close call and inflation risks skew to the upside. Entry levels are more attractive after the pricing pullback.

trade_ideas.description: Long 30y JGB on ASW, entry 45bp, target 35bp, stop 52bp, current 49bp
trade_ideas.rationale: Captures the relative cheapness of long-end JGBs with limited rate risk. Demand is resilient and supply is easing.
trade_ideas.risk: Further position unwinds by non-Japanese investors.

trade_ideas.description: Long 1y fwd 2s10s real €str steepener (entered 25-Sep-26 at 10, target 40, stop -10) and BTPei 41s vs 56s z-spread narrower
trade_ideas.rationale: Oppose large bear flattening priced, and an extreme RV anomaly in BTPei.
trade_ideas.risk: More resilient growth, poorly digested supply of the longer issue.

trade_ideas.rationale: Vol should be supported near term and lower in 2H27 as the US economy fades reflation momentum, led by the left side of the grid.
trade_ideas.risk: Frontloaded cuts or a hawkish Fed medium term.

trade_ideas.rationale: US real-yield breakout resembles Jan-2022, when risk assets topped and macro vol surged.

risk_factors: Rates are not sufficiently restrictive, and a hawkish Fed repricing could pressure vol and spread positions.
Higher rates vol may pressure ASW widening views and cause RV breakdowns and de-risking.
OAT-Bund widening above 150bp could trigger contagion to the periphery and require ECB action.
French growth and feedback loop between financing costs, growth and deficits, with the corporate sector the most fragile.
Fiscal stimulus headlines from Japan's extraordinary Diet session and further unwinds by non-Japanese JGB holders.
US bill supply uncertainty and Fed path uncertainty weaken MMF demand for intermediate bills.
Lower oil prices are a risk to the pay Nov RBA OIS trade.
UK fiscal relaxation is a risk to the long UKT 2033 ASW trade.
Real-yield breakout could repeat the 2022 risk-asset selloff and macro vol surge.

vol_and_positioning: Rates vol repriced higher in September, with both higher forwards and logVol normalization from about 18.1% to about 20.7%. About 11bp of the 21bp rise in 1y10y normal vol is attributed to the logVol reset.

US swaption vol grid is inverted, with the left side rich vs the right. The inversion is modest compared with Mar '26 (Middle East crisis) and Apr '25 (liberation day). 1m2y normal vol is 121 and 30y tails are in the high 80s to 90s.

BofA's baseline is that implieds may ease slightly if yields consolidate, but the market must adjust to a structurally higher vol regime. It sees limited scope for a return to pre-September levels near term.
Vol is expected to remain supported through 1H27, with scope for lower vol in 2H27 led by the left side of the grid, which drives BofA's bias toward receiver calendars.
MOVE index spike coincided with 30y real yields rising since July.
Higher rates hedging flows likely exacerbated the 2s30s steepening move.
BofA's FX and Rates sentiment survey (Sept 4-9) shows steepeners are the most common long-end position in the euro area and US, while Japan investors favor flatteners.
MMFs hold nearly 40% of bills outstanding ex Fed. Indirect bidder demand has weakened for 3- and 6-month bills but strengthened for 1-month bills.
geopolitical: Extraordinary Japanese Diet session begins October 5, with fiscal stimulus headlines possible. A Takaichi administration was reported by Bloomberg on September 15 to be considering raising defense spending to 3.5% of GDP.
A possible Middle East deal is cited as unexpected news flow that could ease rates vol. The report also cites the March 2026 Middle East crisis as a past vol inversion episode.
French political noise and 2027 funding plan concerns contribute to OAT-Bund widening.
US midterm elections in November are a key rates and vol event.

tension_points.bull_case: BofA sees rates not yet sufficiently restrictive, so Fed hike pricing stays elevated and long-end USTs are supported by Fed actions, favoring pay 2Y and flatteners.
tension_points.bear_case: Dovish comments from Williams and Jefferson, a core PCE drop of 3.0% and financial conditions tightening (OAT and US HY widening) could let the Fed move slower and cause bull steepening.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Sept NFP at or below 60k would likely drive a bull steepening and cut terminal Fed pricing to 4.55-4.6%.

tension_points.bull_case: November is a close call and inflation risks skew up, with economists forecasting 3Q trimmed mean at 0.91% q/q and pricing should be closer to 13bp.
tension_points.bear_case: The dovish press conference and downside CPI surprise pared market pricing to 7bp for November and about 36bp by mid-2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Lower oil prices are the stated risk to the pay Nov RBA OIS trade, and a stop is set at 3bp.

tension_points.bull_case: The rise in JGB yields is a global spillover, net supply is falling to ¥5.6tn in Q4, and the 40Y auction bid-to-cover reached 3.10x.
tension_points.bear_case: Global rate pressure and fiscal stimulus headlines from the extraordinary Diet session could push yields up further.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further position unwinds by non-Japanese investors, with the ASW trade stopped at 52bp.
